description: Catalog of hands-on engineering investigations, software craftsmanship, process cinema, and unscripted problem-solving sessions at the desk with Mike Hall.

items.title: Studio Workbench: Hello, World!
items.subtitle: Preparing the workbench, what has gone into it, and working in the open
items.excerpt_or_thesis: Process cinema is not about presenting polished answers as an auteur; it is about working out the problem, discovering what holds together, and learning as you go.
items.topic: Studio Workbench introduction, process cinema methodology, and local toolchain preparation

items.title: Testing the Audio Fix Under the Power Lines
items.subtitle: Field recording, source checks, and audio cleanup
items.excerpt_or_thesis: A phone recording had a loud hum and appeared to be out of sync. Listening to the source showed that the apparent gap was silence after the talk.
items.topic: Field recording, audio cleanup, and checking a proposed repair against the source

items.title: Fluffle: Five Raspberry Pis and 1K+ Transcript Pairs
items.subtitle: A local transcription experiment and where it stopped
items.excerpt_or_thesis: Five Raspberry Pis ran whisper.cpp on more than a thousand Dead Rabbit Radio recordings. The project made useful transcripts, then stopped when its scope grew beyond what Mike could sustain.
items.topic: Distributed transcription, whisper.cpp, and the limits of a small experiment

items.title: The Ship of Theseus: From Wooden Boat to Space Station
items.subtitle: Process cinema and hands-on investigation at the desk
items.excerpt_or_thesis: When an engineer replaces every plank of their personal infrastructure over 15 years, does the identity of the system survive because Theseus directed the substitutions?
items.topic: The Ship of Theseus: 15 years of pipeline evolution, personal tooling, and the builder behind the substitutions

items.title: The Lost Coderwall Guides: Open Source, Vagrant, and What Survives
items.subtitle: Process cinema, open source developer onboarding, and digital archaeology
items.excerpt_or_thesis: When platforms silently lock down historical developer media, how do we preserve the human and technical context of how software was actually built?
items.topic: The Lost Coderwall Guides: 2014 open-source transition, Google Hangouts on Air, YouTube bit rot, and modern system onboarding
